passage: A new girl stood at the edge of the colony play area holding her mother's hand. Saurabh, five, waved from the slide. "Come! You can sit here." He patted the step. "I'm Saurabh. What's your name?" "Anaya." "You can be the driver." His mother Sonali, on the bench, smiled. "Namaste, Anaya, I'm Saurabh's mother." Anaya let go of her mother's hand and climbed up.

qa.q: What did Saurabh offer Anaya?
qa.a: A seat on the step, and the role of driver.

qa.q: What might Saurabh feel toward Anaya?
qa.a: Friendly eagerness, shown by his wave and his offer of a seat. He may also want a new playmate.

qa.q: How did Sonali model welcoming?
qa.a: She greeted Anaya with namaste and introduced herself.

qa.q: How might Anaya feel at the start and then a moment later?
qa.a: Shy at first, then more comfortable, since she let go of her mother's hand and climbed up. 🙂

grounding: Shows a preschooler waving at a new child and offering a seat and a role, with a parent modelling a welcome.

passage:
Hemant, five, ran to the door. "Hi! Come in! You can sit on the cushion."
"I'm Omkar," whispered the boy, half hidden behind his father.
"I'm Hemant. We're building a fort. Do you want to be the guard?"
Omkar looked up at his father, who nodded.
"Okay."
"The guard gets the torch!" Hemant put it in his hand, and Omkar stepped inside.

qa.q: What did Hemant give Omkar?
qa.a: The torch.

qa.q: What might Omkar be feeling at the door?
qa.a: Shy and unsure, since he stayed half hidden behind his father. He seemed more at ease after Hemant's offer.

qa.q: What made it easier for Omkar to join in?
qa.a: Hemant offered a seat and a clear role.

qa.q: How might Omkar's father feel as he nods?
qa.a: Relieved and glad, since he encouraged Omkar to go in.

grounding: Shows a preschooler welcoming a new child by offering a seat and a role in play.

passage:
Note by Irawati, nursery teacher, Monday.
A new girl joined today and stood by the door holding her mother's dupatta. Before I could go over, Parveen walked up, waved, and said, “Hello! I'm Parveen. You can sit next to me.” She patted the mat and offered her the blue crayons, her favourites. The new girl sat down. I had modelled saying hello to every new child at the door, and it seems Parveen was watching. By snack time, the two of them were sharing a paratha.

qa.q: What colour crayons did Parveen offer?
qa.a: The blue crayons, her favourites.

qa.q: What was Parveen feeling when she walked up to the new girl?
qa.a: She seemed friendly and confident, eager to include the new girl, and perhaps proud to copy her teacher.

qa.q: What helped Parveen know how to welcome a newcomer?
qa.a: Irawati had modelled saying hello to every new child at the door, and Parveen copied it.

qa.q: How might the new girl feel when Parveen offers her a seat?
qa.a: She'd likely feel relieved and included after standing shyly by the door.

grounding: The teacher's note shows a preschooler welcoming a new child with a hello, a seat and her favourite crayons, copying what the teacher modelled.

passage: Relatives were coming from the next village, and Varun swept the courtyard. When the cart stopped at the gate, Varun folded his hands. “Namaste, Mausaji! Come, come.” Lalit copied him, hands folded, and then ran to drag a chair over the bumpy ground. “Sit here! It's the best chair!” He waved at the cousins too, jumping. The cousins, shy, hung back. Lalit took the youngest one's hand. “Come see our calf.” Varun smiled. The cousins followed Lalit to the shed.

qa.q: What did Lalit want to show the youngest cousin?
qa.a: Their calf.

qa.q: What was Lalit feeling as he dragged the chair over?
qa.a: He felt excited and eager to make the guests feel welcome, proud to offer the best chair.

qa.q: How did Varun's greeting help Lalit welcome the guests?
qa.a: By folding his hands and inviting them in, Varun modelled a warm welcome that Lalit copied.

qa.q: How might the shy cousins feel when Lalit takes one of them by the hand?
qa.a: They'd likely feel less shy and more included, which is why they followed him to the shed.

grounding: A preschooler copies his father's welcome, offering a chair and inviting a shy cousin to play.

passage: At the kindergarten in Nairobi, a new girl, Nour, stood by the gate holding her father's hand tight. Wanjiru ran over. “Karibu! That means welcome.” She waved both hands. Nour didn't answer. Wanjiru pointed at the sandpit. “Do you want to play?” Nour looked at her father, then nodded. Wanjiru held out her hand. Nour let go of her father and took it. Their teacher, watching, said “Welcome, Nour” at the door, too. By lunchtime, Nour was saying “Karibu” to the next new boy.

qa.q: What does “Karibu” mean?
qa.a: Welcome.

qa.q: What was Nour feeling as she held her father's hand tight?
qa.a: She was probably shy and nervous in a new place, unsure whether to join in.

qa.q: What made Wanjiru's welcome work?
qa.a: She greeted warmly, explained the word and offered a clear invitation to play, holding out her hand.

qa.q: How might the next new boy feel when Nour says “Karibu” to him?
qa.a: He'd likely feel welcomed and less alone, as Nour did that morning.

grounding: A preschooler welcomes a new child with a greeting and an invitation to play, teaching inclusion.

passage:
Every morning Santosh Sir stood at the playschool door, palms together. "Namaste, Lalit!" "Namaste, Sir!"

On Wednesday a new girl hid behind her father's legs, clutching a pencil box. Nobody knew her name. Lalit watched her for a while. Then he walked over, waved with his whole arm and pressed his palms together the way Sir did. "Namaste. You can sit by me. I have the blue chair." The girl peeped out. Slowly, she let go of her father's trouser.

qa.q: What did Santosh Sir do every morning at the playschool door?
qa.a: He stood at the door with his palms together and greeted each child, saying "Namaste".

qa.q: What might Lalit have been feeling as he watched the new girl?
qa.a: He probably noticed she looked scared and felt concerned, wanting to help her in, so he copied Sir's greeting. He may also simply have been curious about someone new.

qa.q: What could Santosh Sir do next to build on Lalit's welcome?
qa.a: He could thank Lalit and ask him to show the new girl the toy corner, so welcoming becomes a class habit.

qa.q: How might the new girl feel when Lalit offers her a seat?
qa.a: She was likely nervous in a strange room, and a friendly child offering a chair can help her feel safer; peeping out shows she is starting to trust.

grounding: It shows a preschooler welcoming a new child by waving, greeting and offering a seat, modelled on the teacher's daily namaste.
